What does the expansion ratio mean?

Expansion ratio compares the distance between the nipples to the width of a single breast base. It helps identify the breast footprint on the chest wall — important for bra wire width selection and surgical planning.

  • Close-set (ratio < 1.2) : Nipples point slightly outward; breasts sit near the centerline. May indicate side-spillage in plunge bras.
  • Standard (ratio 1.2 - 1.5) : Typical "East-West" or "front-facing" pattern. Fits most bra styles.
  • Wide-set (ratio > 1.5) : Nipples point outward; breasts sit toward the sides. Often benefits from side-support bras and push-up styles.
  • High expansion : Significant breast footprint on the chest wall relative to size — may need wider wires.

How to Measure for Pro Expansion Index (Professional Method)

Getting an accurate measurement is the first step to finding a bra that truly fits. Here’s a simple method you can do at home with just a soft measuring tape. No advanced tools needed.

Step 1 — Measure your underbust: Stand upright wearing a non-padded bra. Wrap the measuring tape around your ribcage, just under your bust. Make sure it’s snug but not too tight — that’s your band size (underbust measurement). Write down the number.

Step 2 — Measure your bust: Measure around the fullest part of your bust, keeping the tape parallel to the floor. Don’t pull it too tight — this is your bust measurement. The difference between your bust and underbust measurements determines your cup size.

Step 3 — Use our breast calculator: Enter your measurements into the breast calculator above to get your bra size across US, UK, EU, FR, and AU sizing systems instantly. For the most accurate results, measure first thing in the morning and avoid measuring during your menstrual period when breast tissue may be swollen.

For a more detailed walkthrough, check out our complete guide on how to measure bra size at home .

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the breast expansion ratio?

The expansion ratio is the nipple-to-nipple distance divided by a single breast base width. It describes how spread out or concentrated the breast footprint is on the chest wall. Ratios above 1.5 indicate wide-set anatomy; ratios below 1.2 indicate close-set anatomy.

How do I measure nipple-to-nipple distance?

Stand upright with arms relaxed at your sides. Use a soft measuring tape to measure the straight-line distance from one nipple center to the other, across the chest. Do not measure across the breasts — measure the direct anatomical distance.

Why does breast anatomy matter for bra fit?

Breast footprint determines wire width, gore height, and strap placement. Wide-set breasts often need side-support panels; close-set breasts need plunge or low-gore bras. A correctly identified footprint is the foundation of bra fit.

What is "side spillage"?

Side spillage (or "side boob") is breast tissue that escapes under the arm and beyond the wire. It is common in wide-set breasts wearing narrow-wire bras. A wider wire or side-support panel resolves most cases.

Is expansion related to breast size?

Not directly. A small-breasted woman can have wide-set anatomy, and a large-breasted woman can have close-set anatomy. Expansion is independent of cup size — it is a footprint measurement.

What is a healthy nipple-spacing ratio?

A ratio below 0.45 is typically considered minimal splaying. Ratios between 0.45 and 0.55 are within the average range. Values above 0.55 may indicate more pronounced splaying, which can affect bra fit—bras with wider gores and side-support features are often more comfortable.

How do I measure shoulder width?

Stand upright with relaxed shoulders. Have someone measure the distance between the bony points at the outer edge of each shoulder (the acromion processes). Alternatively, measure from the shoulder seam of a well-fitting shirt.
